It starts only on Play (never by itself), Pause stops it, and nothing moves while still, a picture that arrives late included (drawn once, then the same pixels): the journeys the-preview-draws, the-preview-plays, the-preview-shows-the-picture and the-preview-is-still (2.2.2).

hover-focus-content.evidence: CORE-05 (2026-11-22): the page shows two pieces of content on hover or focus, both Carbon's tooltips: Help's "Close" (its close button's) and the timeline thumb's value words ("0:00 of 0:02"); nothing else on the page shows any (probed: Help, the link, the play bar's three buttons, the switch). The journey content-on-hover-or-focus (tests/a11y/project.mjs) shows each by focus and by hover and finds each hoverable either way (the pointer moved onto its content and rested 1 s, past Carbon's 300 ms leave delay, still shown; shown by focus, focus unmoved; the pointer leaving again while focus stays is not claimed) and persistent (held 1.5 s; its content no longer drawn once the focus or the pointer goes); each is dismissed by one Escape (its content no longer drawn, whatever its words) with the pointer unmoved, focus kept and nothing else changed, except Close's tooltip shown by hover with focus elsewhere in Help, which is credited by 1.4.13's exception: it obscures nothing (its box and caret meet no words where they show, the dialog's heading "Help" among them, and no control or image but Close, measured at the run's width and at 320 px; "where they show" is judged by what is painted: two pictures of each overlap with the tooltip unpainted, with and without the words' parent or the control; equal pictures, nothing of it shows there; the measure checks the page under the tooltip is still and leaves the tooltip shown and the pointer unmoved). There one Escape closes Help, focus back on "Help" (Carbon's Modal and Tooltip both hear Escape on the document; ruled with D195, provisional), and the journey pins it. The thumb's tooltip covers part of the label "Timeline" while the thumb has focus; one Escape hides it. Measured on Help only: a later dialog with a longer heading, or anything placed beside Close, must be measured again.

keyboard-shortcuts.evidence: CORE-05 (2026-11-21): the editor listens for its keys on the page (src/editor/shell/keydown.ts, dispatch.ts, keys.ts): Space plays or pauses, Home and End (and < and >) skip to start and end, comma and full stop step one frame back and forward (D205, 2026-11-24), Cmd or Ctrl with Z undoes and with Shift redoes, and the keys of one printable character the table names (J, K, L, comma, full stop, < and >, and ? for Help) are live while their switch, "Single-key shortcuts" in Help, is on, as the page opens, and do nothing while it is off (D183; src/editor/shell/Help.tsx, held for the visit in session.ts). Help, a button after the paragraph, opens a dialog (src/editor/kit/Dialog.tsx) listing every shortcut. The play bar after Help (src/editor/shell/PlayBar.tsx), "Skip to start", "Play" and "Skip to end", calls what Home, Space and End call; with nothing to play Space, K, J and L say why and start nothing, and Play is disabled and described by that reason. Journeys: character-key-shortcuts (2.1.4, both ways), fields-and-status (3.3.5, 4.1.3), reading-and-focus-order (2.4.3), pointer-cancellation (2.5.2), keyboard-task (3.2.2); keyboard functions skip-to-start-by-home, skip-to-end-by-end, open-help-by-button, open-help-by-question-mark, close-help-by-escape, single-keys-off, single-keys-on, skip-to-start-by-button, skip-to-end-by-button-space-kept, play-refused-by-space, play-refused-by-k and play-refused-by-k-, -j- and -l-on-button The timeline, a slider in the play bar (src/editor/shell/Timeline.tsx), keeps its own keys: the arrows move it, with Shift four times as far; Home and End on it go to its start and end, and Page Up and Page Down a tenth of it up and down (the kit's slider takes them, D193), saying nothing; the single keys on it say what they say elsewhere, and nothing while their switch is off.

canvas.evidence: CORE-05 (2026-11-23): the editor draws its preview on a canvas (src/editor/shell/Preview.tsx), in a box that is an image named "Route animation preview" (1.1.1, the reviewed snapshot); nothing in it could be operated until CORE-06. CORE-06 (2026-11-25, brief 112): the box is a toolbar with one tab stop (an application since brief 114, D245), and its canvas takes the pointer: the pen's tap places a point on the up-event, joined from the selected one, and Escape clears the selection; pointer-cancellation reads it while a press is held, after a press moved off and after a whole press (2.5.2). CORE-06 (2026-11-26, brief 116): a point on it is dragged by the pointer; point-drag-moves reads the dragged point's marker at its new place, not at its tap, after the release, and at its tap again, not at the new place, after one Undo, and point-drag-escape reads the whole canvas as before the press after Escape mid-drag and after the release that follows (2.5.2). The point's drag has no single-pointer alternative yet (2.5.7 owed, D250). CORE-06 (2026-11-26, brief 117, D252): in pen-drawn only, the preview's set-aside carries a measure (tests/a11y/project.mjs, PEN_DRAWN_ASIDE; run by contrastRows in tests/a11y/helpers.ts after the state's other contrast readings): skipped to the route's end, the line, both points' markers and the selected point's ring, each pixel composited over the box's own background and its ratio taken against it, each at 3:1 or it fails 1.4.11, as does a measure that reads nothing. It claims only the plain background with no picture in pen-drawn at the default settings; the user's own picture and routes in their own colours stay set aside (1.4.11, essential), and the other states that show the preview keep the set-aside unmeasured. No row of the catalogue is triggered by this feature alone. CORE-06 (2026-11-26, brief 119, D208; brief 120; brief 121, ruling AD): with the route selected, an idle mouse or pen on a line draws its stretch with a white and blue halo, the line redrawn over it in its own colour, and an insert handle (a "+") at the line's middle; a tap on the "+" inserts a bend there. line-insert-plus, in pen-drawn skipped to the route's end, first reads the hover with no press, as regression checks that earn nothing by themselves: three tenths along the line, its centre pixel in the line's own colour and a pixel beside it in the halo, both as before once the mouse leaves the preview, then the "+" drawn active with the mouse on it. Its 2.5.2 credit rests on the press, the up, Undo and the abort alone: a press on the "+", held, leaves the whole canvas as before; the up draws the new bend's grey dot at the middle; one Undo draws the whole canvas as before; a press on the "+" moved 45 px off it and released there adds no point, and one Redo then draws the undone bend again, so the abort made no step (2.5.2). It claims nothing for 1.4.11 (the halo and the "+" stay under the preview's set-aside), 1.4.13, 2.5.7 (still owed, D250) or 2.5.8 (the "+"'s target size, D255). CORE-06 (2026-11-26, brief 122, rulings AH and AJ): Cmd+click on a point (Ctrl+click elsewhere) adds it to the selection or takes it out, never a step, so a plain press on one of several selected points drags them all. group-drag, in pen-drawn skipped to the route's end with the selection cleared by Escape, first reads the selection's ring at each tap (the pixels drawn and not the route's hue 5 to 9 px from it) as each point is picked, one taken out and put back, which earns nothing by itself. Its 2.5.2 credit rests on the abort, the up and Undo alone: a press on the second point moved past the threshold and aborted by Escape leaves the whole canvas as before the press, and the release after it changes nothing; pressed, dragged and released, both points' markers are drawn at their new places and neither at its tap; one Undo draws the whole canvas as before the drag (2.5.2). A group's drag is a second dragging movement on the preview with no single-pointer alternative yet, under the same 2.5.7 debt as a point's (D250). It claims nothing for 1.4.11 (the rings stay under the preview's set-aside), 1.4.13 or 2.5.8. CORE-06 (2026-11-26, briefs 123 and 124): with points selected, Delete or Backspace deletes them, Cmd+D (Ctrl+D elsewhere) copies them 2% of the picture right and down as one step and Cmd+A (Ctrl+A) selects every point. edit-keys, in pen-drawn with focus moved to the preview box by Tab, End and Escape pressed there, does the three edits with keys alone: Cmd+A rings both points (the ring's pixels, read as group-drag reads them); Cmd+D rings a copy 2% right and down of each, the originals still drawn (the copies draw no marker of their own, since the lead's walk does not reach them, so their ring is what is read); one Undo draws the whole canvas as before it; Cmd+A then Delete leaves neither marker nor the line; one Undo draws the whole canvas as before it; focus stays on the box (2.1.1). Its claim is only that these three edits are done from the keyboard alone: drawing points is still a pointer's (the pen's tap), and it claims nothing for 2.5.7 and nothing spoken (D263). CORE-06 (2026-11-26, briefs 125 and 126): with points selected, an arrow moves them 0.5% of the picture over the zoom, Shift with it 2%, held on the picture, and a run of presses less than 400 ms apart is one undo step. nudge-keys, in pen-drawn begun as edit-keys begins, then Cmd+A, nudges with keys alone: ArrowRight three times moves both points' rings 1.5% of the picture right, neither ring left at its tap; one Undo draws the whole canvas as before the three; Shift+ArrowDown moves the rings 2% lower; after a wait past 400 ms, ArrowLeft and one Undo draw the canvas as after Shift+ArrowDown (2.1.1). Its last step, ArrowRight, a pointer press on the page's header and ArrowRight inside 400 ms, then one Undo drawing the canvas as after one ArrowRight alone, checks that a press on the page ends a run (the page's own listener) and adds nothing to the claim. The keys' claim, edit-keys' and nudge-keys', is only that the three edits and the nudge are done from the keyboard alone: drawing points is still a pointer's, it claims nothing for 2.5.7 (a point's single-pointer move is the point's menu item Move, still owed, D250), and nothing is spoken (D263). CORE-06 (2026-11-27, brief 132, D266, the owner's "Full colour, dashed"): the guide drawn while the preview is not playing (D265) is the route's colour at full alpha, still 2 wide and dashed 6 on and 4 off. PEN_DRAWN_ASIDE's measure first presses Skip to start, where nothing of the line is drawn yet and only the guide draws between the taps, and reads 25 places along the line, each the most opaque of the 7 pixels across it: some must be the route's hue and some bare (the box's background shows), or it gives no ratio; the most opaque of the route's hue, composited and taken against the box's background by the measure's formula, at 3:1 or it fails 1.4.11: rgba(213, 94, 0, 255) against rgb(244, 244, 244), 3.52:1; with the half alpha it replaced put back, rgba(213, 94, 0, 128), 1.86:1, and 1.4.11 fails. It claims only the guide in the default colour on the plain background with no picture in pen-drawn; the guide over the user's own picture, or in their own colours, stays set aside. CORE-06 (2026-11-27, briefs 135 and 136, D267 (a) and D269, provisional): the point's menu. The journey point-menu, in pen-drawn with focus on the box: a right-click on a point shows a menu named "Point actions" in document.body, outside .preview, its menuitems "Mark as start", "Mark as end", "Set lead start" (aria-disabled, described by "This point is already where the lead starts."), "Make bend" and "Delete" (a separator before it), the point selected; focus is on its first item on opening, and after Escape, an item chosen and at the end it is on the box (2.4.3); Shift+F10 on the box opens it; ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End move and wrap; Escape closes it with the point still selected; "Make bend" by Enter draws the point's grey dot (3 dark pixels within 2 px, 0 as a stop) and one Undo the canvas as before; "Mark as start" makes the menu read "Remove start mark", undone by one Undo; "Set lead start" on the lead's start stays open on Enter, Space and a click and changes nothing; "Delete" removes the point and its line and says "Point deleted" (2.1.1); over the run the status said, in turn and each once, "Point made a bend", "Undo", "Start marked", "Undo", "Point deleted", "Undo" (D269's words; the disabled item says nothing); in a window 200 px high End reaches "Delete" inside the window, a wheel over the menu scrolls it and leaves it open, and a scroll of the page outside closes it. Each of eight faults fails it: the menu mounted inside .preview, focus not returned on Escape, an item that is off still run, "Make bend" not dispatched, the menu's maximum height removed, a scroll inside the menu closing it, "Make bend"'s words left out, a second "Point deleted" said. Its name and roles are read and fail the journey, but it claims nothing for 4.1.2 (the catalogue lists only axe, lint and a snapshot for 4.1.2, and the runner refuses a journey's claim on it), nothing for 2.5.7 (the menu's "Move" is still owed, D250) and nothing for the marks' drawing: no drawing reads a route's marks yet.
